title: McGill 1988: centroid distance of psoas major at L4-L5 (M, supine)

imaging.plane: single transverse slice with the gantry tilted to the plane of the L4/L5 disc

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm; area centroid

source.authors: McGill SM, Patt N, Norman RW
source.sample: 13 active men; men referred for diagnostic CT (most with low back pain/sciatica), screened for activity level

how_to_simulate: In the plane through the L4/L5 disc (parallel to it), take the PCSA-weighted centroid of the right-side muscle (or the named portion).
Report X (lateral) and Y (AP, + anterior) from the disc centroid; compare with mean +/- SD. Centroid distance, not a moment arm.

subject_model.source: Table 1 (SD age 11.9, height 5.9, weight 11.7); disc area 19.0 (2.4) cm2 Table 2

protocol.notes: Right side only. Disc centroid lies at 57.2% of trunk depth from the anterior surface. cm -> mm.

extraction.check_notes: Average/SD row re-read from text of Table 6; signs as printed (erector negative = posterior).
